about: Cross-lingual retrieval probes. Moved out of retrieve/crosslingual_check.py in Part 6 so that expectations are reviewable data rather than code. Every probe states what it asserts and why; `expect_text_contains` exists because a probe that asserts only expect_doc can pass against the wrong passage of the right document.

non_english.note: Every non-English language in the corpus. Used as the candidate pool for cross-lingual probes so an English query cannot be satisfied by an English translation — which would make the probe a same-language test wearing a cross-lingual label.

probes.name: greek query -> greek Periplus (Muziris)
probes.query: Μουζιρὶς καὶ Νέλκυνδα ἐμπόρια τῆς Λιμυρικῆς
probes.note: Can the model see Greek script at all? Failure here means nothing downstream is interpretable.

probes.name: chinese query -> Weilue Da Qin
probes.query: 大秦國在安息西，海西之地
probes.note: Literary Chinese, no word spaces. The corpus holds only two Chinese chunks, so this is a thin measurement.

probes.name: tamil query -> Akananuru 149
probes.query: யவனர் முசிறி பொன்னொடு வந்து கறியொடு பெயரும்
probes.note: Old Tamil scored 0.368 in Part 4 against 0.6-0.7 for other scripts. It still ranked first, but with one Tamil chunk in the corpus that number means little. Recheck when Tamil coverage grows.

probes.name: parthian query -> SKZ
probes.query: šāhān šāh Ērān ud Anēran Šābuhr
probes.note: Romanised Parthian, not its own script. Tests whether scholarly transliteration survives the tokenizer.

probes.name: english query -> greek source (frankincense at Kane)
probes.query: the frankincense-bearing country and the port of Kane in Arabia
probes.note: The claim the project rests on: an English question reaching a Greek source with no English in the pool.

probes.name: english query -> greek source (Adulis ivory)
probes.query: the port of Adulis and the ivory brought to the Aksumite capital

probes.name: english query -> chinese source (Roman embassy)
probes.query: an envoy sent by the king of Da Qin, the Roman empire
probes.note: English to Literary Chinese, two writing systems with no shared vocabulary. Scored 0.472 in Part 4.

probes.name: english query -> parthian source (Roman provinces)
probes.query: the Roman provinces of Cilicia, Cappadocia, Syria and Galatia
probes.note: The ŠKZ §20 province list is direct Rome-contact evidence in Parthian.

probes.name: paired EN: Muziris and Nelkynda ports
probes.query: the ports of Tyndis, Muziris and Nelkynda and the kingdoms they belong to
probes.note: Originally asked about pepper and failed — correctly, because pepper is §56 and the record then held only §53-54. The corpus did not contain the answer being asked for. The probe was fixed to ask what §53-54 says; the corpus was separately extended to §56, and the pepper question became its own probe.

probes.name: paired GRC: Muziris and Nelkynda ports
probes.query: Μουζιρὶς καὶ Νέλκυνδα καὶ Τύνδις, βασιλεῖαι τῆς Λιμυρικῆς
probes.note: Same question as the probe above, in Greek. Both must rank the expected document first AND agree with each other.

probes.name: english query -> greek source (pepper cargo at Muziris)
probes.query: large ships loading pepper and malabathrum from Kottanarike
probes.note: The passage-level assertion is the point. Without it this probe reported PASS against §53 while §56 was not in the database.
